hero.prompt: Use case: scientific-educational. Asset type: revised 16:9 editorial cover illustration for a rigorous review of the Riemann hypothesis, the quasi-Riemann hypothesis, and AI-assisted mathematical proof. Input image: edit target and palette reference only. Primary request: replace the vague glass architecture with a clearly recognizable mathematical scene of the zeta function's critical strip and nontrivial zeros. Keep the restrained deep navy, teal, ivory and warm gold palette, but completely replace the current perspective corridors, glass walls and decorative particle clouds. Compose an elegant front-facing complex-plane-inspired mathematical illustration, almost orthographic, not a room: one large vertical translucent teal critical strip with clearly visible left and right boundaries; within it a single very thin luminous gold vertical center line. A modest number of distinct gold zero markers lie exactly on that center line, with deliberately irregular spacing both above and below a subtle horizontal midline; leave a clear gap at the horizontal crossing so there is no marker at the real-axis crossing. The central line and zero markers must be the immediate focal point and remain clear at thumbnail size. A broad softly illuminated interior band conveys the wider region still allowed by a quasi-Riemann result, distinctly broader than the single central line; subtle narrow darker side bands within the strip hint at excluded regions. Add just a few restrained smooth oscillatory wave traces approaching from the dark side margins to suggest the link to prime-counting oscillations; keep them visually distinct from the zero markers. Use fine sparse coordinate-grid traces, mathematical editorial precision, subtle depth and paper-like luminous texture, generous quiet space, strong simple hierarchy. This is a symbolic conceptual illustration, not measured zeros, a numerical zeta plot or a proof; do not imply that the whole Riemann hypothesis has been proved. No text, letters, numerals, equations, labels, legends, logos, watermarks, people, robots, brains, circuit boards, photorealistic laboratory hardware or architectural glass corridors. Exact aspect ratio 16:9.
hero.claim: A symbolic critical strip, central line and nontrivial-zero markers make the Riemann-hypothesis subject visible. The line is a conjectured general zero location; markers, bands and waves are not computed data or a proof. Precise 7/8 and 11/12 boundaries are shown only in the deterministic figures below.

deterministic_figures.method: Original explanatory diagrams generated by matplotlib; text outlined
deterministic_figures.basis: The 7/8 manuscript and the 11/12 alternate manuscript; functional-equation symmetry for the Riemann zeta function.
deterministic_figures.claim: Candidate regions for nontrivial zeros, including boundary lines, conditional on the stated manuscript claims. Not a numerical zero search. The RH line remains conjectural.

deterministic_figures.method: Original teaching calculation of x^(beta-1), plotted by matplotlib
deterministic_figures.basis: beta = 11/12, 7/8 and 1/2; Fiori–Jaskari, arXiv:2609.23222v2, Theorem 1.4, for the separately computed normalized bound.
deterministic_figures.claim: Pure power factors exclude zero heights, constants, logarithms, epsilon losses and the full zero sum. They are not observed prime-counting errors or complete error bounds. The two normalized conditional bounds are teaching calculations, not proof verification.
